posts.author: DJ Mathson
posts.content_md: Does anyone know where it it possible to get hold of a couple of Panasonic LNCQ05PS laser diodes? They are not available at Optima-Optics anymore and I can´t find them anywhere else. Or have someone found any better option than the Panasonic diode? The Mitsubishi diode seems to be a bit unreliable.

posts.author: tpark
posts.content_md:
> **DJ Mathson:** Does anyone know where it it possible to get hold of a couple of Panasonic LNCQ05PS laser diodes? They are not available at Optima-Optics anymore and I can´t find them anywhere else. Or have someone found any better option than the Panasonic diode? The Mitsubishi diode seems to be a bit unreliable.

If you're near a hop zone, the LNCQ05PS can be unreliable too, but I've generally had good results with that panasonic device. I have had good results with the ML1016R after getting it away from a hop zone, and driving the device with a constant current driver. 

[http://www.thorlabs.com/ProductDetail.c ... t_ID=36213](http://www.thorlabs.com/ProductDetail.cfm?DID=6&ObjectGroup_ID=7&Product_ID=36213)

This diode looks promising, but I haven't purchased or tried it yet. It looks like it can put out 80mw, 658nm of eyeball cooking laser light, but I suspect you can run it at lower power, probably resulting in shorter wavelength and somewhat less coherence length. I think you need an external photodiode if you want to have a constant power setup, however I suspect it might be better to use constant current and go way below the maximum rated power.

On another note, are there recommendations for a 635 nm diode out there? I haven't tried too many of the 635 nm lasers, but I haven't had good results with the ones I have tried.

--Ted

posts.author: Tom B.
posts.content_md:
Too bad Optima dropped the LNCQ05 - I'd better take good care of mine. Relative to most electronic components, laser diode distribution is strange - I can't find an alternate distributor either. Maybe you could call Panasonic? 

A possible alternative is the Sharp GH06550B2B 50 mW 654 nm diode, available from [http://www.digikey.com](http://www.digikey.com) for $74.03 each. The Digikey catalog number is 425-1807-ND. They show 2503 in stock. I have not tried this diode, but intend to someday.

data sheet:

[http://www.sharpsma.com/sma/Products/Op ... 550b_e.pdf](http://www.sharpsma.com/sma/Products/Opto/data/pdf/en/ld/laser_diodes/gh06550b_e.pdf)

Given the rate at which DVD burners are dropping in price, it might be cheaper just to buy a burner and rip out the laser diode. (Only half joking)

posts.author: John Klayer
posts.content_md: The Sharp GH06550B2B is one of the choices available for the Analog Technologies mode hop free laser.
